- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to pivot; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment reversal by +1–3% in the 5–7 day window.
- Model tends to overestimate short-term (1–3 day) volatility when sentiment is volatile; dampen forecast variance by 10–20% in such cases.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is negative or neutral over 5+ days.
